task: Fix degraded single-host review fallback so Proof-or-stop requires mechanical host availability proof before accepting lower-assurance fallback.
outcome: When the user runs `lattice review_escalation_fallback_set --storyId=<id> --eligibility=single-host-environment ...` on a machine where codex and claude are executable, the terminal rejects it with text like `fresh host availability probe shows 2 available canonical hosts; use full 3x2 or explicit-human-approval`, and `lattice review_escalation_status --storyId=<id>` says degraded fallback is invalid until a fresh probe proves fewer than two hosts or explicit human approval is recorded.
facts: 2026-07-09 user identified that codex, claude, and agy CLIs are available on this machine, contradicting a single-host fallback claim.
Current review_escalation_fallback_set validates eligibility/reason/evidence/hash but does not mechanically probe canonical host availability.
Review assurance floor and review escalation DONE gates consume degraded fallback process events, so this is a gate-consumed process fact bug.
Canonical hosts from dev-memory are Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, and Antigravity CLI via agy; codex+claude are preferred, agy is fallback.
Chosen design is a new review_host_availability_probe command that records structured process evidence consumed by fallback handlers and DONE/status evaluators.
constraints: Do not use operator prose as proof for single-host scarcity.
Do not claim degraded 3x1 equals full 3x2 or Authority completion.
Register new gate-consumed process facts in process-fact-levels/process-fact-registry and contract verification.
Keep explicit-human-approval available as explicit lower-assurance fallback with approvalRef.
Do not redesign the full cross-host runner or remote release path.
